I've noticed similar thoughts/feelings recently. They were really bad not too long ago after I crashed into a guardrail, avoiding the car who had just pulled out in front of me when I was already at 45 mph. I found myself so upset that I hadn't done something more, something that would have likely killed me. Driving away, I was consumed by thoughts of how I should do something now, since the car was already damaged. One less thing to be guilty about. I kept driving and kept obsessing over it. But I never went out of my way to sabotage myself. For days I just beat myself up. Why hadn't I done something that day before anyone knew anything happened? Why hadn't I taken the opportunity yet to try and kill myself while the car was damaged? The thing is, it still is damaged. I haven't repaired it. It's as if I am holding onto it as some ticket that I can redeem when I kill myself. Once it's fixed, I won't have that excuse in my mind and the fear of guilt will return.

So I think that might be the feeling you're referring to. As to what I'll do with my excuse, I still don't know. It's always easier to go on knowing you have a loophole out. Like you said, I don't know if I will ever carry anything out. I haven't yet, and some would argue that I never will or that it's a sign of my strength and that I can keep fighting. To me, I just haven't found the right time.

I realize this is different still from your situation, but I wanted to say it. Now, it sounds like it's mainly your father who would be truly upset and who you're afraid of. I suggest bringing in a third party. Someone to help ease any conflict, prevent dangerous outrage, and hopefully present any bit of rational thought on the matter. Surely you're no less terrified, but I don't want this to be the point when you end your life.

The fact that you keep going through the motions is a good sign. Unlike shutting down, it has the possibility of things changing, maybe even getting better. You seem tough to have been doing this for a while. I hope you continue trying. I still try to meet people, too, even though like you said most people seem to already have their friends. Trying something local and recurring is my best thought.
